timeline.text:
A quick update from Newport Beach on the coastal flooding impacting our communities.

Thankfully, it appears the worst is behind us, thanks in large part to the tireless efforts of our local emergency response crews.

But a flood advisory remains in effect, and elevated tides continue to pose risks along our coastline. Please exercise caution and follow local safety guidance.

Governor Newsom’s emergency order remains in place, and my office will keep pushing to ensure Orange County receives the state and federal resources our communities need.

Over the summer, we learned that several servicemembers and civilians who worked at Fort Meade tragically died by suicide. One loss of life is one too many – and that is why I am committed to doing everything we can to make sure everyone at the Fort has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again. Here is an update on that work:

✔️In last year’s defense bill, I worked with colleagues to secure a provision requiring U.S. Cyber Command and the Cyber Mission Force to hire mental health professionals with security clearances at their operating locations. 

✔️I am now leading my Maryland delegation and Armed Services colleagues to help secure $11 million in funding needed to ensure full funding of this provision.

✔️I am also committed to working alongside U.S. Cyber Command to bring additional mental health resources to Fort Meade. I’m working to rectify the reporting requirements and include civilian employees in DoD’s suicide data, especially at installations like Fort Meade where civilian and uniformed officers work side by side on the same projects.

✔️Finally, I am working to address delays with the transfer of mental health licenses from out of state. During conversations with mental health professionals, I heard that the transfer of licenses can take several months to almost a year before these professionals can begin practicing in Maryland and on military bases. At the state level, I am working with partners, including @SenatorDawnGile and Secretary Ed Rothstein of the @MdVeterans, to address delays and barriers to military-connected mental health professionals transferring or obtaining professional licensure in Maryland.

This is just the beginning – and structurally addressing the gaps in mental health services and availability will be an ongoing effort. I will continue to keep you posted as we move this work forward together.
